problem.claim: Learn accurate long-horizon geometric horizon models for future-state prediction and planning without compounding rollout errors.

gap.claim: Existing generative TD-style methods for GHMs are impaired by training-time bootstrapping and struggle with high-quality long-horizon predictions.

contributions.claim: Introduces TD-Flow, combining a Bellman equation on probability paths with flow matching to learn GHMs.
Establishes a new convergence result and attributes TD-Flow’s efficacy primarily to reduced training gradient variance.
Shows that similar arguments can extend to diffusion-based methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a novel Bellman equation on probability paths and uses it with flow matching for TD-based GHM learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that TD-Flow learns accurate GHMs at over 5× the horizon length of prior methods.
The authors report validation across diverse domains using generative metrics and downstream tasks, including policy evaluation.
The authors report substantial performance gains when TD-Flow is integrated with recent behavior foundation models for policy planning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Future prediction supports agent reasoning and planning, but stepwise world-model inference can compound small errors.
GHMs avoid cumulative inference errors, yet existing generative TD methods suffer from bootstrapping and weak long-horizon generation.
TD-Flow applies a probability-path Bellman equation with flow matching; the paper reports a convergence result and reduced gradient variance as a main explanation.
The paper extends similar reasoning to diffusion methods and reports broad metric, task, and planning evaluations with substantial gains in the latter setting.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a training-dynamics explanation—reduced gradient variance—to a method designed for longer-horizon prediction, then reports both generative and downstream-task evaluations.

lessons.interpretation: Aligning a mechanism-level explanation with evaluations at both the representation/output level and the intended decision task makes the contribution easier to assess.
lessons.application: For a long-horizon prediction paper, state the hypothesized optimization mechanism and pair generation-quality measurements with a downstream planning or policy task.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work has no credible mechanism hypothesis or no meaningful downstream use case.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the convergence conditions or theorem details.
The prior-method baselines, domains, metrics, task results, and numerical size of the reported gains are unspecified.
The meaning of “over 5× the horizon length” and the scope of the diffusion extension are not detailed.
